source.title: Decode-gLM: Tools to Interpret, Audit, and Steer Genomic Language Models
source.authors: Aaron Maiwald; Piotr Jedryszek; Florent Draye; B. Schölkopf; Garrett M. Morris; O. Crook

record.tranche_reason: Tests the hierarchy component of V3 using a meta-SAE trained on SAE decoder weights, rather than testing feature splitting across dictionary sizes.
record.gate_note: The 50M versus 500M comparison reports counts and F1-scores of interpretable latents, but does not vary SAE dictionary size or map features between dictionaries. Those results do not test the claimed splitting pattern. The relevant result is the reported grouping of HIV-related SAE latents by a meta-SAE.
record.test_reason: The study applies a meta-SAE (from Leask et al.) to decoder weights of a single BatchTopK SAE (one dictionary size, expansion 8) on Nucleotide Transformer 500M. It reports that one meta-latent (#107) groups five HIV-related child latents. Those latents are distinct HIV elements (RRE, DIS, psi, PBS, Env), not finer splits of one coarse feature. No dictionary-size sweep, no cross-dictionary feature matching, and no geometric-closeness measure are reported. The result is hierarchical grouping among latents of one SAE, a related but different construct from splitting. It is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test of V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors say meta-SAEs recover hierarchical structure and that the model 'encodes concepts at different levels of generality'. This rests on one highlighted HIV-related meta-latent (#107) aggregating RRE, DIS, Psi, PBS and Env latents.
record.recipe_differences: Uses BatchTopK SAEs on Nucleotide Transformer activations and a meta-SAE trained on SAE decoder weights; it does not sweep SAE dictionary size or test feature correspondences between dictionaries.

fits_no_version.finding: A meta-SAE latent (#107) on a 500M Nucleotide Transformer SAE activates on five HIV-related child latents. Its encoder row as a probe scores 57.2% F1 on the combined HIV annotations versus ≤44.8% for any individual annotation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Meta-SAEs trained on SAE decoder weights recover higher-level concept groupings among latents of a single SAE, here in a genomic language model.

record.problems: The hierarchy evidence is a reported result for one highlighted meta-SAE latent and one annotation set; no uncertainty estimate is stated. It does not measure geometric closeness or feature splitting across dictionary sizes.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported result directly measures a claim version. The model-size comparison and counts of interpretable latents do not test dictionary-size splitting or feature correspondence.

untested.parts: No dictionary-size sweep and no mapping of coarse features to finer ones.
No splitting analysis in any model or open SAE release.
No split features, no nesting across dictionary sizes, no geometric-closeness measure. Meta-SAE grouping of single-SAE latents is related but not the same claim.
No parent/child firing coverage, and no size or sparsity effects on absorption.
Meta-SAE is used but there is no comparison of larger versus smaller SAE latents, novel latents or completeness.
No comparison of training objectives and no artifact analysis.

record.verdict_notes: Overturned the reader's 'tests/T2/V3 supports'. The study never varies dictionary size, and the grouped latents are distinct sibling elements rather than splits of a parent feature. The evidence is one selected latent with no uncertainty, and code is not yet released. The 50M vs 500M comparison counts interpretable latents (135 vs ≤65) and bears on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No increasing-dictionary-size sweep or mapping of a smaller-dictionary feature to several larger-dictionary features.
Does not test the splitting pattern across large models or open SAE releases.
Tests semantic grouping into a higher-level concept, but not geometric closeness, nested splitting across dictionary sizes, or whether the families mirror a broader model hierarchy.
Does not test parent-child activation coverage or the effect of SAE size or sparsity on absorption.
Does not compare larger- and smaller-SAE latents for decompositions, novel latents, or completeness.
Does not test whether splitting is an artifact of the SAE objective or compare objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs.

rows.subject: Nucleotide Transformer (500m)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated meta-SAE latent #107's encoder row as a linear classifier for HIV-related annotations.

conditions.value: hold-out test set of 500 annotated plasmid sequences

rows.measure: F1-score for the combined HIV-related annotation set
rows.baseline: F1-score for any individual annotation was ≤ 44.8%.
rows.note: The meta-SAE latent was reported to activate on child latents associated with RRE, HIV-1 DIS, HIV-1 psi, HIV PBS, and envelope proteins. Its combined-set F1-score exceeded the score for any individual annotation; the authors interpret this as a higher-level HIV-related concept.
rows.check: Measures probe F1 of one meta-SAE latent's encoder row on combined HIV annotations (57.2%) versus any individual annotation (≤44.8%). It concerns grouping of latents from a single SAE, not split features across dictionary sizes or their geometric closeness, so it does not bear on V3 as stated. The latent is a hand-picked 'striking example'; no count of such meta-latents and no uncertainty are given.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Meta-SAE latent #107 on the tested HIV-related annotations
reader_labels.reason: The meta-SAE grouped several HIV-related child latents, and the combined annotation set scored 57.2% F1 versus ≤ 44.8% for any individual annotation (R1), supporting semantic higher-level grouping in this setting.
